definition: Watkins v. United States, 354 U.S. 178 (1957) is a U.S. Supreme Court case holding that he Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment limits Congressional authority to require testimony on inquiries unrelated to the charge for which Congress had summoned the witness to testify. In response to the Red Scare of the early-1950s, the House of Representatives created the Committee on Un-American Activities to investigate links (real or perceived) to the Communist Party. The Committee issued a subpoena to John Watkins, who worked as a labor union organizer, to appear as a witness to clarify allegations that he was a member of the Communist Party. Watkins denied allegations that he was a member of the Communist Party to the Committee’s satisfaction, but the Committee then inquired into other people Watkins knew and whom the Committee believed to be communists. Watkins refused to answer the Committee’s roving inquiry on people he knew, objecting that “I [do not] believe that this committee has the right to undertake the public exposure of persons because of their past activities.” The Committee initiated a prosecution to hold him in contempt ,and the Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia upheld his conviction of one year in prison and a $100 fine for contempt. Watkins petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court for a writ of certiorari, which the Court granted. The Supreme Court, in a 6-1 opinion written by Chief Justice Warren, overturned his conviction, finding that Congress’ roving inquiry violated Watkins’ procedural due process rights of the Fifth Amendment. The Court conceded that a witness could be held in contempt for refusing to answer a Congressional Committee’s questions if the questions are intended to assist with conducting a specific legislative task. However, as a matter of jurisdiction, a Congressional Committee only has the authority to inquire into matters pertinent to the legislative tasks delegated to them. The Court noted that the Committee’s task was vague and unclear, making it difficult to determine the particular congressional function.
